quotes.text: The problem lies in the model. Passwords were designed decades ago, an era of local systems and small networks. Today's Internet operates on a scale that relies on global connectivity, distributed apps, and millions of identities.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes password breaches as a design flaw of the model rather than a user discipline problem.

quotes.text: Passkeys are powered by public key cryptography. The private key stays on the user's device, while the server only holds a public key. That means nothing sensitive ever travels across the network or has to sit in a database waiting to be stolen.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in plain terms why passkeys remove the stolen-secret attack surface.

quotes.text: Servers only hold public keys, and those alone can't be reversed into valid credentials. The credential theft marketplace loses its raw material, breaking the cycle of reuse and resale that drives so many breaches today.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why a breached passkey database is worthless to attackers.

quotes.text: The key is to have recovery clearly planned and tested before passkeys are rolled out at scale, so users aren't stranded when something goes wrong.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete rollout recommendation that is often overlooked in passwordless projects.

quotes.text: With passkeys, there is nothing to rotate or expire, which means those reset tickets simply disappear from the queue.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Ties passkeys directly to a measurable help desk benefit.

chapters.title: The real cost of broken passwords

takeaways: Passwords fail because the model itself is outdated, so stricter policies and rotations cannot fix phishing, credential reuse or reset overhead.
Passkeys built on WebAuthn keep the private key on the user's device and store only public keys on the server, which removes stolen credentials as an attack surface.
ASP.NET Core teams can add passkey registration and login endpoints with existing libraries, then prove the value with a small pilot that measures reset tickets and incidents.
hook: Phishing, credential stuffing and endless password resets keep draining security teams and help desks. This episode is for developers and IT leaders who want to replace passwords with passkeys and WebAuthn in ASP.NET Core and Microsoft 365 environments. You get a clear implementation checklist, a better user experience and a pilot plan to measure real ROI.
